plans.note: Section 21 holds the full liability regime: 21.1 mutual cap (greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000), 21.2 consequential-damages exclusion with direct-damage carve-ins, 21.3 Excluded Claims definition, 21.4 savings language. Check mutuality, cap size and whether confidentiality/data/security, indemnity, gross negligence and IP infringement are carved out; also confirm payment obligations are unlimited.

Vendor IP indemnity at 20.1 and conduct/data/law indemnity at 20.2; Customer's reverse indemnity at 20.3 (test that it stays narrow and excludes Vendor Technology/combination); procedure at 20.4; infringement remedies at 20.5, cross-referenced by 9.3. Confirm indemnities are carved out of the cap via 21.3.

Section 12.3 expressly preserves Customer's freedom to develop, buy, or build anything and disclaims any non-compete; this benefits us. Scan Sections 2 and 12 for any conflicting restriction before concluding compliance (note the exclusivity language at 2.2 is handled under EXCLUSIVITY, not double-flagged here).

Section 2.2 (first of two clauses numbered 2.2) makes Vendor the sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services for the term — directly contrary to our position and in tension with 2.1 and 12.3. Primary redline target; note the internal conflict with 12.3's no-exclusivity acknowledgement.

Section 7.2 (first clause so numbered) obliges Customer to give Vendor terms no less favourable than those offered any other technology supplier — an MFN running against us. Section 12.3 disclaims any MFN commitment; cite that conflict when proposing deletion.

Section 12.4 binds Customer for eighteen months post-termination, covers any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term, and bars engagement as well as solicitation with no general-advertising carve-out. Test against the fallback on duration, personnel scope and the recruitment carve-out preserved in 12.3.

Section 9 provides only for-cause, insolvency and security/service-failure termination; no convenience right for either party appears. Confirm nothing in 8.1-8.2 or an Order Form mechanic supplies one before treating as missing; note 27.3 gives a force-majeure exit and 10.2 a refund mechanic that would support a convenience right.

Section 8.2 auto-renews Order Forms for twelve months on 180 days' notice — test the notice window against the preferred/fallback thresholds. Section 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice, which supports compliance on pricing predictability.

Section 28.1 selects New York law and disapplies the CISG; 28.2 gives exclusive jurisdiction to New York County courts (not foreign arbitration); 28.3 adds a short executive escalation that does not bar urgent relief. Verify against the accepted-law list.

24.1 gives us free assignment to Affiliates and successors; 24.2 restricts Vendor assignment and change of control; 24.3 residual consent standard; 24.4 bars Vendor from terminating or repricing on our change of control. Cross-check the licence transfer right in 13.3, which references Section 24.

14.1 confirms Customer ownership of Customer Data and pre-existing IP; 14.2 assigns Deliverables to Customer on creation subject to payment; 14.3 preserves Vendor Technology with the 13.2 perpetual licence; 14.4 handles joint IP and feedback. Check the definitional carve-outs in 1.3, 1.4 and 1.8 and the no-training/no-sale restriction in 15.1 for any leakage of our data or IP to Vendor.

13.1 grants Affiliate and contractor access for internal business purposes; 13.2 gives a perpetual paid-up licence for delivered Vendor Technology; 13.3 limits revocation/suspension to material uncured breach after notice and cure; 13.4 sets use restrictions. Confirm no at-will revocation and that restrictions in 13.4 do not undercut permitted use.

Section 22.1 permits Vendor audits at any time without notice with remote access to our systems — fails notice, frequency and off-site requirements. 22.2 and 22.3 partially mitigate (Vendor bears cost absent >5% underpayment; no direct system or unrelated data access; findings are our Confidential Information); redline 22.1 to add notice, annual frequency and business-hours limits consistent with 22.2.

Section 7.6 imposes USD 25,000 per day liquidated damages on Customer for any delay in providing a dependency — a penalty running against us and uncapped in practice. Primary redline; consider interaction with the liability cap in 21.1 and the dispute-withholding right in 7.3.

19.1-19.3 give workmanship, conformity (90 days for Deliverables, full term for hosted Services), malicious-code, legal-compliance and no-functionality-reduction warranties; 19.4 gives repair/re-perform then terminate-and-refund, expressly non-exclusive for IP, confidentiality, privacy and security. Check duration and remedy against the parametric thresholds; acceptance remedies at 6.1-6.2 are supporting context.

Section 18.1 sets CGL, workers' comp, employer's liability, E&O and cyber limits with a one-year tail; 18.2 addresses insurer quality, certificates, cancellation notice and non-limitation of liability. Verify the cyber and E&O limits meet the required minimums for a vendor hosting Customer Data.

Section 2.1 expressly disclaims any minimum quantity or purchase commitment and confirms non-ordering is not a breach; 12.3 repeats the no-minimum-volume acknowledgement. Favourable to us; check 7.1's bar on undisclosed minimum-use charges for consistency.

Section 11.1 gives up to six months of transition assistance at expiring-Order-Form rates for termination for any reason; 11.2 requires data return within thirty days in machine-readable form with no fee-dispute hostage; 11.3 covers certified deletion. Cross-check 10.1-10.2 (post-termination rights and refunds) and 16.5, which defers to Sections 11 and 15 for Customer Data.
